Announcements - Faculty Senate President Nassersharif offered remarks about theFaculty Senate budget, noting that the Faculty Senate leadership, including committeechairs, are faced with the difficult task of balancing Senate service with their regularfaculty duties.

Any time thatthe Senate has required additional resources, members had to make a special requestfrom the Provost.
Without a budget model that provides for adequate and reliablesupport, the Senate’s autonomy and ability to engage in shared governance fully has beencompromised.

Announcements and Budget Presentation - The President highlighted someevents and gatherings around campus so far this year.
Of special note were eventsinvolving Hillel and the Middle Eastern Students Association in response to thecrisis in Gaza.
President Parlange emphasized the need to foster a welcomingcommunity at URI where everyone feels respected and free to speak without fear.Fall events also included a very successful Quad Fest, coinciding with the AnnualDay of Giving, which exceeded all fundraising expectations.

President Parlangemoved on to address URI’s global rankings and praised US News and WorldReport for revising their methodology.
This has resulted in a number of publicuniversities, URI included, moving up in rank.
In terms of the annual budget presentation, the President noted that while URIdid not get everything it asked for from the State of RI, its allocation did increasefor 2024, which gives the university some momentum to carry out someimportant initiatives.
Increased state funding comes in the form of the standardbudget allocation as well as special funds (ARPA, bonds, etc).
President Parlangethen outlined spending priorities for the year, including essential services, capitalprojects, and certain strategic investments.
The university is transitioning to anincentive-based budget model which will be new for the URI community.
It is theBOT’s and the administration’s position that this model will reward innovationand entrepreneurship, improve transparency and accountability, and incentivizeimproved academic quality. c.

Informational Report on Curricular Processing Timelines - Chair Preisserdeferred to Faculty Senate Specialist Genvieve Spitale to present the report.
The report made clear that the CASC is a very hard working group, havingreviewed 142 course proposals last academic year.
Of those, 140 wereapproved and 91% were acted upon by the Faculty Senate at the meetingimmediately following the CASC meeting.
It was hoped that this datawould help to dispel the myth that the Faculty Senate approval process iscumbersome and slow.
Most proposals spend the majority of their reviewtimeline under the purview of the departments and colleges involved, i.e.before they reach the level of the Faculty Senate and its committees.Proposers need to keep in mind that review workflows arecollege-specific and timelines can vary a great deal from college tocollege.
The Faculty Senate office is in the process of modernizing its webpages and curricular processing deadlines will be clearly posted to helpproposers better manage their schedules and expectations. ii.
